title: performance: perf-canary automated detection + rollout guards (adaptive thresholds, hysteresis)
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Adds adaptive auto-detection for performance canaries and rollout guards with hysteresis to prevent flapping. Improves detection sensitivity for p95 latency and throughput regressions and adds automated rollback triggers.
description: Motivation: Production rollouts have been repeatedly impacted by transient latency spikes and noisy metrics which caused either missed regressions or frequent rollback churn. This PR implements an adaptive auto-detection pipeline for the performance canary service and introduces hysteresis-based rollout guards so canaries only fail when regressions are persistent and statistically significant. What changed: 1) New detector: perf-canary/auto_detector.py implements background metric smoothing (EWMA) + z-score anomaly scoring for p50/p95 latency and throughput on a per-model, per-route basis. 2) Adaptive thresholds: defaults.yaml exposes sensitivity and min-sample-window and the detector updates thresholds dynamically using baseline windows and confidence intervals. 3) Hysteresis rollout guard: perf-canary/rollout_guard.py enforces consecutive-window gating and cool-down periods (min_fail_windows, cool_down_secs) to avoid flapping. 4) Integration with traffic shifter: small integration in redwood/serving/routing/traffic_shifter.py to automatically trigger rollback or pause traffic shift when guard trips. 5) Tests and docs: added unit tests (test/perf_canary/test_detector.py) and user-facing docs (docs/perf-canary.md). Compatibility: works with existing canary pipeline and observability stack (Prometheus metrics and traces). Backwards compatibility: config keys are additive and default to conservative values so existing canaries behave unchanged until enabled. Operational notes: detector runs as low-priority background job with CPU/lightweight math only; all thresholds and decisions are exported as metadata to the canary event stream for auditability. Related: ENG-4123 implements earlier telemetry changes used by this detector. Checklist: - [x] detector implementation - [x] rollout guard logic - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] docs and runbook entry - [x] canary pipeline integration - [x] manual canary dry-run and benchmark run (no regressions observed)
commits: 1) Implement EWMA+zscore detector and config defaults; 2) Add hysteresis-based rollout_guard and cooling policy; 3) Integrate guard with traffic_shifter and add metadata export; 4) Tests + docs + small refactor to metrics names
diff_snippets:
perf-canary/auto_detector.py (snippet): def update_baseline(window): ewma = alpha*sample + (1-alpha)*prev; z = (sample - mean)/std; if z > sensitivity_threshold: mark_anomaly();
perf-canary/rollout_guard.py (snippet): if consecutive_fail_windows >= cfg.min_fail_windows and time_since_last_change > cfg.cool_down_secs: trigger_rollback(reason="perf_canary_regression")
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a few inline notes around the EWMA alpha tuning and edge cases for cold-start windows. Suggest adding a min_samples guard to avoid spurious z-scores.
Ava Thompson (author): Addressed Diego's notes — added min_sample_window and switched default alpha to 0.2; added comment and test for cold-start behavior.
Priya Rao: Approve after minor docs tweak - request to highlight that detector exports decision metadata for audits.
Samir Patel: Ran integration canary. Observed one false-positive under bursty load, but hysteresis prevented rollback. Approving.
ci_checks: perf-regression-bench: pass (no regression detected on internal staging)
notes_for_release: Enable by setting perf_canary.autodetect.enabled=true and tune sensitivity via perf_canary.autodetect.sensitivity. Default behavior is conservative; recommended to run in passive mode for 1 week before enabling active rollback.
manual_verification: Performed dry-run on staging with traffic-shift simulation and a controlled latency injection test; detector flagged the regression and guard suppressed immediate rollback until condition persisted for 3 windows. Operator ran manual rollback to validate path.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: algorithmic sensitivity tuning required per-customer workload. Risk mitigated by conservative defaults, hysteresis, and metadata auditing.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): add adaptive auto-detection and hysteresis-based rollout guards to reduce flapping and detect persistent perf regressions
